counterexample.failure: For every nonzero epsilon the density is nonzero and periodic in x^1 and independent of x^0,x^2,x^3. The curvature-square action is infinite, while the background action is zero. Its finite-parameter density difference is noncompact. Nevertheless its pointwise first derivative at epsilon=0 is zero, exactly as the corrected compact first-variation interface requires.
counterexample.geometricScope: All metrics are smooth Lorentzian and conformal to Minkowski, hence the example also remains within smooth globally hyperbolic geometry if a consumer requires that stronger scope.

localityProof: Each curvature-squared density coefficient is a smooth finite-jet function of the inverse metric on the nondegenerate matrices. Curvature uses at most two coordinate derivatives. Joint smoothness permits exchanging parameter and spatial derivatives; the first derivative is a finite sum of smooth coefficient functions times derivatives of h through order two. It therefore depends only on h and vanishes off supp h. This gives a compact smooth density whose integral is finite, without exchanging an infinite integral and derivative. Different families with the same inverse-metric tangent have identical first-variation densities. A compactly supported affine inverse-metric family realizes each h on a sufficiently small common interval by openness on its compact support.
scopePreserved: All originally admitted smooth families with compactly supported h remain admitted, including h=0 families with arbitrary higher-order noncompact changes. No restriction to compact backgrounds or finite total actions; no stronger Choice assumption.
